grammatical_complexity.notes: Dialogue format keeps many sentences simple, but the second half is dense with modal perfects, conditionals, and past perfect. Complex structures appear in roughly 25-30% of sentences.

cultural_reference_load.notes: Most references are understandable from context or globally known. 'Community college' and 'child support' are North American institutional concepts but inferable. 'Oompa loompa' requires pop culture knowledge but doesn't block comprehension.

sentence_structure.notes: Dialogue format creates a mix of very short exchanges and longer compound-complex sentences. Ken's summary speech near the end contains sentences over 30 words with multiple subordinate clauses.

items.context: Actually, I wanted to talk to you guys about that.
items.reason: Spanish speaker may read 'actualmente' (currently) and be momentarily confused, though context of the conversation provides some disambiguation.

items.context: I only ever saw him once.
items.reason: Context of seeing someone 'once' is clear; the number meaning (eleven in Spanish) doesn't fit.

items.context: I quit my job and found work somewhere else shortly after.
items.reason: Context of leaving a job makes the meaning clear; 'quitar' (to remove) doesn't fit.

items.context: 2 months passed and I realized I was pregnant.
items.reason: Context of becoming aware of pregnancy is unambiguous; 'realizar' (to carry out) doesn't fit.

items.context: Whatever respect I had for you, mother, has now completely disappeared.
items.reason: Spanish 'respeto' also means esteem/regard, so this is not a true false friend in this context.
